audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer says Purgatory only matters 'once he reaches you' (spikes[2]) and that your kite 'offsets his fresh ult before he ever closes the gap' (spikes[1] and whys[4]). Purgatory is a thrown artifact with 1000 range — it does not require him to close anything.
audit.why: Teemo's whole plan against Locke is spacing. Telling the player that spacing beats the ultimate is the one wrong conclusion that gets him killed at 6, because he will hold position at a distance the ability covers comfortably.
audit.corrected: Purgatory reaches 1000 — further than his Q at 950 and much further than your 680. Distance does not save you from it; HP above the execute floor does.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer says 'everything hinges on Blinding Dart timing' and 'a landed blind is a won trade' without ever saying why blind is unusually strong in this specific matchup.
audit.why: Locke is one of the few matchups where blind is worth its cooldown, and for three separate reasons at once: Silver Stake is on-hit, so blind removes it; the Ritual Nails marks are cashed by his attacks, so blind stalls the payoff; and Ashen Pursuit ends in an attack, so blind blanks the arrival. A reader given the reason will time it correctly instead of guessing.
audit.corrected: Blind here denies three things in one cast: the Silver Stake on-hit, the attack that consumes his nail marks, and the attack Ashen Pursuit lands on arrival.
sources: champ-data/_kits/locke.json (P on-hit; Q 'consume the marks to deal bonus damage with his attacks'; E autoReset 'dashes to attack his next target')

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Silver Stake's damage increases based on your missing health.
audit.why: It compounds with the Purgatory execute: the lower you are, the harder his autos hit, which pushes you toward the execute floor faster. That is the actual shape of the danger curve and it explains why 'chip patiently' is right early and suicidal at low HP.
audit.corrected: Silver Stake scales on your missing health. Every point you drop makes his next attack bigger, and the execute is waiting underneath.
sources: champ-data/_kits/locke.json (P Silver Stake: 'increased based on enemy missing Health')

audit.whatIsWrong: Soul Ignition (W) is never mentioned in either layer. It grants attack speed and move speed, damages Locke himself, and heals a portion of that damage back only at the END of the duration.
audit.why: The heal is back-loaded, which is a real exploitable window: pressure applied during Soul Ignition is paid for in advance, and if the fight ends or he disengages before the duration expires he never collects. It is also the anti-heal target flagged for this matchup.
audit.corrected: Soul Ignition heals him only when the effect ends. Grievous Wounds applied before that moment is worth far more than the same anti-heal applied afterwards.
sources: champ-data/_kits/locke.json (W: 'At the end of the duration, Locke will heal back a portion of the damage he takes during the effect')

audit.whatIsWrong: 'mid' tells you to hold the blind 'for the moment he starts his slow-in'. Ashen Pursuit is a teleport followed by a dash — it is instant, not slow. The slow in his kit is on Ritual Nails (Q) and Purgatory (R).
audit.why: There is no wind-up to react to. Blind cannot be held for a tell that does not exist; it has to be pre-committed to the arrival or spent on the mark-cashing attack.
audit.corrected: Hold it for the attack on the other side of his E, not for a telegraph.
sources: champ-data/_kits/locke.json (E Ashen Pursuit; Q and R carry the slow flags)

audit.why: The full layer's 'ten seconds after each spent blink' matches Ashen Pursuit's cooldown exactly — 10 at every rank, a single value in the kit. Good number, correctly used.

49.53% over 860 games is the largest sample in my slice and both layers correctly present the matchup as even with Locke taking the level-6 and first-item stages. This is the one matchup in my slice where the two level charts are broadly consistent with each other.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2] ('Hold your self-peel strictly for his blink') and dontsFull[2] ('Fight inside the totem below a quarter HP') carry descriptions copied from other slots — dosFull[2].d is a full-commit cue and dontsFull[2].d is the tradeBad string verbatim.
audit.why: The Don't about fighting at low HP inside Purgatory is the most important line on the page and its explanation is about nail marks instead.
audit.corrected: Give each its own mechanic: the back-loaded Soul Ignition heal, and the missing-health scaling that feeds the execute.

notes: Best-authored entry in my slice by a distance: the FULL layer for Locke is clearly hand-written (correct ability names, real cooldowns, a coherent mark-count thesis) and I found nothing wrong with it beyond two mismatched dos/donts descriptions. All my work here went into the CONTENT layer, which is thin and generic by comparison ('his damage window', 'his on-hit pressure') and never names an ability or a number. FLAG ON THE TOOLING, NOT THE DATA: champ-data/_kits/_missing-interactions.json lists 'resistances-invalidated — Locke bypasses stacking resistances (Soul Ignition (W))' for this matchup. That is a false positive. Reading W's own description, the only damage in Soul Ignition is damage Locke deals to HIMSELF; there is no enemy-facing true damage, so the trueDamage flag should not have generated a 'raw armour or MR is the wrong answer' headline. I did not write that claim into the data. The same derived-flag looseness appears on Teemo's own R, which carries a knockup flag it does not deserve — Noxious Trap slows, it does not displace — so the 'knockup-enabler' pairings involving Teemo R (the flagged teemo-vs-kled and teemo-vs-malphite ones) should not be trusted either. Champion-wide name defects still outstanding: "Blinding Shot" x271 and "Liandry's Angueur" x80 in champ-data/content/teemo.js. Worth noting this Locke entry already uses the correct "Blinding Dart", so the bad name is not universal in the file — a global replace is still safe, it just will not touch the bespoke entries.
